title: Control verdict
description: The Level 1 verdict of a repository: one of four words for every requirement, one overall result, and a digest of the control register and the evidence file it was computed from. The file is written by `lisa controls attest` and is never edited by hand; `lisa controls attest --check` computes it again and fails when the two differ.

result.description: `conforming` only when every requirement is `conforming` or `not-applicable`. A requirement that is `unknown` prevents it.

prevented_by.description: The requirements that prevent a conforming result, in the catalogue's order. Empty exactly when `result` is `conforming`.

criteria.description: One verdict per in-scope requirement, in the catalogue's order.

evidence_as_of.description: When the newest evidence record was completed, or `null` when there is no evidence.

current_until.description: The first instant an evidence record this verdict rests on stops being current, or `null` when it rests on none. From then on the verdict is out of date and the check fails.

criterion_id.description: A requirement id as the specification writes it, for example `AC5.4` or `SI7`.

utc_time.description: A time in UTC with milliseconds, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ`.

sha256.description: A SHA-256 digest in lower-case hexadecimal, taken over the canonical text of a JSON value: object keys in code-unit order at every depth, no spaces, lists in their own order.

rung.description: How strongly something is known, weakest first: `asserted` (said, not checked), `observed` (a setting read from the system that holds it, or a file found where the audit pointed), `exercised` (a change was planted and the control's answer recorded).

requirements.description: Which requirements the verdict was computed against.

specification.description: The specification the requirements were taken from.

level.description: The conformance level the verdict is for.

sha256.description: The digest of the requirements catalogue itself.

counts.description: How many requirements came out as each word.

digest.description: What binds the verdict to the files it was computed from.

value.description: The digest of the two together: of the object `{ "evidence": <the evidence file>, "register": <the register> }`.

verdict.description: `conforming`: everything that answers it held, on evidence strong enough for it; `rung` says how strong, so a reader can tell a proof from a located file from a person's word. `non-conforming`: a control that serves it failed, or the audit found nothing that does it. `unknown`: there is no evidence, the evidence is out of date, or it is weaker than the requirement needs. `not-applicable`: it does not apply, and `fact` says why.

reason.description: A short, fixed word for why.

detail.description: The same as a sentence for the operator, with what to do about it where something can be done.

kind.description: What sort of thing answers the requirement, from the catalogue: `gate`, `artifact` or `human-attested`.

minimum_rung.description: The weakest evidence the requirement accepts, from the catalogue.

rung.description: The weakest rung a `conforming` verdict rests on; `null` on any other verdict.

entries.description: The register entries that serve the requirement, in register order.

evidence.description: The identifiers of the evidence records the verdict was read from, in order.

fact.description: The fact that makes the requirement `not-applicable`, as the audit gave it; `null` on any other verdict.
